sentences.text: Camposaurus was a small, carnivorous theropod dinosaur estimated to reach a length of 3 meters.

Like other coelophysids, this animal possessed fused tibio-tarsals and fibulo-tarsals, but it had a distinct ridge at the back of the tibia where it fits with the fibula, a feature unlike its relatives.
The holotype specimen UCMP 34498 was discovered in 1934 in the Placerias quarry of the Bluewater Creek Formation in Arizona.

The type species Camposaurus arizonensis was formally named and described in 1998 by Adrian Hunt, Spencer G. Lucas, Andrew B. Heckert, Robert M. Sullivan, and Martin Lockley. The genus name means "Camp's lizard" and honors Charles Lewis Camp, while the species name refers to the fact that the dinosaur was found in Arizona, United States.
Analysis demonstrated that Camposaurus is definitely a neotheropod belonging to the parent group Coelophysinae and the family Coelophysidae.

In 2000, Downs examined the remains and concluded it was a junior synonym of Coelophysis. A 2007 review by Nesbitt et al. noted that the ventral astragalar margin was straight and indistinguishable from that of Coelophysis bauri. Many paleontologists have rejected Camposaurus as a nomen dubium due to the lack of material. However, a reassessment by Ezcurra and Brusatte revealed two autapomorphies in the holotype, firmly establishing Camposaurus as a valid genus and species. A 2011 phylogenetic analysis found Camposaurus to be a close relative of Megapnosaurus rhodesiensis. A 2017 phylogenetic analysis found the synonymy with Coelophysis unsupported, placing Camposaurus in a clade with Megapnosaurus, Segisaurus, and Lucianovenator.
